To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
explicit instructions and large perturbations lead to increased awareness of the perturbed movement, but not to changes in the sensory and motor consequences of movement.

explicit instructions and large perturbation sizes can lead to awareness of the perturbations during motor adaptation, but that the resulting changes in sensory and motor representations are not dependent on this awareness.

explicit instruction and large perturbations both increase explicit awareness of the perturbations but do not increase the magnitude of implicit learning, and that proprioceptive recalibration is largely independent of awareness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of learning and the factors that influence the learning of new motor skills.
the effects of awareness on motor adaptation.
understanding how explicit instruction and awareness affect motor learning and the sensory consequences of movement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
explicit instructions are beneficial for motor learning, but only in the early stages of training and only for the updating of efference copy based estimates of sensory consequences.
explicit awareness of the perturbations during motor adaptation can lead to improved performance, but only during the initial phase of learning.

explicit instructions and large perturbation magnitudes lead to a larger and faster learning-induced shift in hand localization estimates, which are based on both proprioceptive recalibrations and updates in the expected sensory consequences of movement, and that these effects persist for up to 90 trials of adaptation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
awareness of a perturbation can be beneficial, but it may not always be the most effective strategy for learning.
explicit instruction can be useful for learning to counter the rotation, but it has little impact on the implicit processes of proprioceptive recalibration.
awareness of the perturbing force does not affect the learning induced recalibration of sensory estimates of hand position.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of awareness are not uniform across the different processes that are engaged during motor learning.
explicit instruction and awareness can be used to accelerate learning, particularly during early adaptation, but that the effects of explicit instruction on proprioceptive recalibration are minimal.
awareness of the perturbations during adaptation can lead to a more efficient motor learning, but it does not affect the underlying mechanisms that drive motor learning.
